title: Consistency of a mixed layer depth operator with each model's own mlotst output
science_question: Does a mixed layer depth computed from a model's own temperature and salinity fields reproduce the mlotst that the same model publishes, and where does it not?
query:
Check whether a mixed layer depth (MLD) computed from each CMIP6 model's own temperature and salinity reproduces the mlotst field that the same model publishes. This is an internal consistency test: both quantities come from the same simulation, so any disagreement is a property of the diagnostic, not of the model's physics.

Data to use:
- CMIP6 historical `thetao` (potential temperature), `so` (practical salinity) and `mlotst` from CESM2, GFDL-ESM4 and MPI-ESM1-2-LR, monthly, 1971-01 to 2000-12.
- Each model's own published cell areas (areacello) for every area weighting.

All of it stays on each model's native grid. CESM2 and MPI-ESM1-2-LR are curvilinear, so the fields must never be sliced by latitude and longitude value, and nothing is regridded at any point in the calculation; the operator MLD and the published mlotst already sit on the same grid, which is what makes the comparison a like-for-like one.

Follow this procedure exactly.

1. Operator MLD, month by month. For each model and for each individual month of March and of September in 1971-2000, that is 30 Marches and 30 Septembers, compute the MLD from that month's `thetao` and `so` using a potential density threshold of 0.03 kg/m3 measured against the model's shallowest level as the near-surface reference depth. All three models describe their mlotst as sigma-T referenced to the ocean surface, so the reference depth is the shallowest level and not the 10 m used by observational climatologies. The crossing depth is interpolated between the bracketing levels rather than snapped to a level.

   Compute the MLD separately for every month and only then average. The MLD of an averaged temperature and salinity profile is not the average of the monthly MLDs and is systematically shallower, because averaging smooths away the pycnocline; averaging the profiles first is the main way this calculation goes wrong.

2. Climatological fields. For each model and each of the two calendar months, average the 30 operator MLD fields into one climatological field, and average the 30 published mlotst fields the same way. A grid cell enters either climatology only if it has a valid value in all 30 years; a cell missing in any year is left out of both.

3. Bias and error. For each of the six model-and-month combinations, report over the whole global ocean:
   - the area-weighted mean difference, operator MLD minus mlotst, in metres to 1 decimal place;
   - the area-weighted root-mean-square difference in metres to 1 decimal place.
   Weight every cell by the model's own areacello, and take both metrics over the cells where the two climatological fields are both defined.

4. Spatial correlation. For each of the six combinations report the area-weighted spatial Pearson correlation coefficient between the operator MLD and mlotst climatological fields, to 3 decimal places, over the same cells.

5. Where the two disagree. For each of the six combinations report the percentage of ocean AREA, not of grid cells, on which the absolute difference exceeds 20 m, to 1 decimal place. Take the percentage over the area where both fields are defined, and also report that shared area as a percentage of the model's total ocean area, so that any cells dropped in step 2 are visible.

6. Summary. State which model is most internally consistent and which least, and name the regions where the disagreement concentrates. Then explain why the operator and mlotst are not expected to agree exactly even though both come from the same simulation: say how the model computes its own mlotst differently from the operator applied here, and which way that difference should push the bias.

Produce two figures.

Figure 1, a 3-by-2 panel of global maps of the difference field, operator MLD minus mlotst, with rows for CESM2, GFDL-ESM4 and MPI-ESM1-2-LR and columns for March and September. All six panels share one diverging colour scale centred on zero. The two curvilinear models cannot be drawn directly on a latitude-longitude axis, so for DISPLAY ONLY put each difference field on the common 1-degree grid; every number reported in steps 3 to 5 must still come from the native grid, and the figure must say so.

Figure 2, a 3-by-2 panel of scatter plots in the same row and column layout, each with the operator MLD on the x axis and the published mlotst on the y axis, one point per ocean cell of that model's native grid. Use logarithmic axes on both, because mixed layer depth spans from a few metres to a few thousand, give every panel an identical axis range and identical ticks, and draw a dashed y = x reference line in each. Annotate each panel with its bias, its root-mean-square difference and its correlation.

expected_numeric_outputs.definition: area-weighted mean of (operator MLD minus mlotst) over the shared valid cells, on the model's native grid weighted by its areacello
area-weighted root-mean-square difference between the two climatological fields over the same cells
area-weighted spatial Pearson correlation between the two climatological fields
percentage of the shared ocean AREA on which |operator MLD minus mlotst| exceeds 20 m
the area where both fields are defined, as a percentage of the model's total ocean area
the three models ordered from most to least internally consistent, with the criterion used stated

expected_figures.content: operator MLD minus mlotst for each model (rows) and March/September (columns) on one shared zero-centred diverging scale, regridded to 1 degree for display only
operator MLD on x against mlotst on y, one point per native ocean cell, logarithmic axes with identical ranges and ticks, a dashed y=x line, each panel annotated with bias, RMSD and correlation

grading_notes: The single most important trap is the order of operations: the MLD must be computed for each month and then averaged. Computing one MLD from the 30-year mean temperature and salinity gives a systematically shallower field and different numbers throughout.

The reference depth must be the model's shallowest level, not the 10 m of the de Boyer Montegut observational criterion. All three models publish mlotst as sigma-T referenced to the surface. For CESM2 and MPI-ESM1-2-LR the two choices happen to give identical results because of where their shallowest levels sit, but for GFDL-ESM4, whose shallowest level is 2.5 m, the March 1971 bias moves from -10.0 m to -7.6 m.

The density threshold is 0.03 kg/m3, the CMIP6 protocol's value: OMIP defines mlotst by a buoyancy difference of 0.0003 m s-2, which it equates to 0.03 kg/m3 and attributes to Levitus (1982) (Griffies et al. 2016, Appendix H24). The larger 0.125 kg/m3 used in some studies deepens the mixed layer: at 0.125 kg/m3 the March 1971 RMSD rises from 18-39 m to 60-90 m in every model (the reference answer reproduces this check). An answer that uses 0.125 will be wrong by a large margin and should say which threshold it used. Calling 0.125 'the Levitus criterion' conflicts with the protocol's own attribution and should not be rewarded.

Everything is computed on the native grid with each model's own areacello. Regridding first would replace those areas with the target grid's and change every number; the regridding in figure 1 is for display only.

Step 5 asks for a fraction of AREA, not of grid cells. On a curvilinear grid the two differ substantially, because cell size varies by more than an order of magnitude between the tropics and the poles.

Cells where the operator MLD is undefined, because the density threshold is never reached in a column that is mixed to the sea floor, are genuinely missing rather than zero. They must be excluded from both climatologies and from the denominator, and the shared-area percentage is what makes that exclusion auditable. Excluding them is required, not merely convenient: the models' own mlotst encodes those columns differently. Checked on March 1990, GFDL-ESM4 and MPI-ESM1-2-LR report roughly the full column depth there (median mlotst/deptho 0.96 and 0.85), while CESM2 reports 0 m in most of them (1077 of 2486 cells, largely on Arctic shelves), so no single fill value would be fair to all three.

The residual is expected to be systematically NEGATIVE (operator shallower than mlotst) in every model, and a good answer says why. The protocol computes mlotst online at every time step, from a surface parcel moved to each level's own pressure, and archives the monthly MEAN of those instantaneous depths (Griffies et al. 2016, H24). The operator here takes a sigma0 difference on the monthly-mean profile, and a monthly mean is itself an averaged profile, so the same smoothing that makes a 30-year-mean profile too shallow also makes a monthly-mean one shallower than the mean of the instantaneous MLDs. The ranking of step 6 must be read with one further caveat: GFDL-ESM4 computes mlotst on its native 75 hybrid layers (top layer 2 m), but its archived thetao and so were remapped to 35 z levels and regridded to 1 degree, so part of its larger disagreement is the archive's vertical resolution rather than the model. An answer that reads the residual as a model physics error has misread the case.
